description: An unnarrowable key falls back to joining all of the type's accessors — not to a blanket floor. A type whose accessors are all clean stays clean; get and set are still joined separately, so writing through a throwing setter is reported where reading the same member is not.

diagnostics.message: Reading `throwingGet[key]` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it runs the getter `b`, whose body was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try`/`catch`, or make the getter `b` non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.

Writing `throwingSet[key]` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it runs the setter `a`, whose body was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try`/`catch`, or make the setter `a` non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.
